Slots.maps_to: `Encounter.slots` (monsters/base.py) -- `FAKE_MERCHANT_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` (fake_merchant.py:119-124) passes no `slots=`, so it defaults to `()`, where FakeMerchantEventEncounter.cs:17 declares `["merchant"]`. Slots.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). The `Encounter` dataclass already had `slots`/`monster_slots` and `CreatureCmd.add(slot_name=)` re-sorts on them (shipped round 7 for Fabricator/Ovicopter); this unit simply never declared its row. It does now, transcribed from the C# `Slots` override and `GenerateMonsters`' `(model, slot)` pairs, and `CombatState.__init__` routes every roster through `Encounter.seat_in_slots` so the seventeen `create_monsters` overrides are seated too. WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_slots_not_ported (same mechanism as dense_vegetation_event's Slots/GenerateMonsters entries): the single `"merchant"` slot is not represented. Traced the one consequence (`CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name`, no-ops on empty `slots` and is never called for initial roster construction anyway) and the only OTHER thing slot identity could matter for -- move-selection or any other behavioural branch on `FakeMerchantMonster.slot_name` -- reading FakeMerchantMonster.cs and fake_merchant.py's `FakeMerchantMonster` class top to bottom finds no such branch on either side. Costs nothing for a single fixed monster with no slot-conditioned behaviour.

guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `Encounter` gained an explicit `entry_slug` field and `Encounter.entry` returns it when set, so this unit seeds `make_encounter_rng` with the game's real `ModelId.Entry` while keeping its sim id. A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one.
